title: Counting: measure words, 几, 每, 半, 万, money, 有的 / 一些, 什么都
description: The common measure words, 'several' with 几, every (每), half (半), ten thousand (万), prices, 'some', and 'anything / everything'.

points.title: Measure words
points.summary: Number / 这 / 那 + measure word + noun. Common ones: 本 (books), 张 (flat things), 件 (clothes, matters), 杯 (cups of), 条 (long things: roads, trousers, fish), {只|zhī} (animals).
points.body: - 两**件**衣服, 三**张**纸, 一**杯**咖啡, 一**条**裤子.
examples: I bought two pieces of clothing.

points.title: 几 + measure word: several
points.summary: In a statement, 几 + measure word = a few, several.

points.title: 每 + measure word (+ 都): every
points.summary: 每 + (measure word) + noun, usually with 都 before the verb.

points.title: 半: half
points.summary: 半 + measure word = half a …; number + measure word + 半 = … and a half (一个半小时).
points.body: - **半**个小时 (half an hour), 一个**半**小时 (an hour and a half).
examples: I waited an hour and a half.

points.title: 万: ten thousand; money
points.summary: Chinese counts in 万 (10,000): 五万 = 50,000. Money: 块 (spoken) / 元 (written) + 毛 (0.1). 三块五 = ¥3.50.

points.title: 有的 vs 一些: some
points.summary: 有的 + noun = some (of a group), often contrasted: 有的…，有的…. 一些 + noun = some, a few (amount).
points.body:
- **有的**人喜欢茶，**有的**人喜欢咖啡.
- 我想买**一些**水果.
examples: {有的|yǒude}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{茶|chá}，{有的|yǒude}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{咖啡|kāfēi}。
Some people like tea, some like coffee.

points.title: 什么 / 谁 / 哪儿 + 都: everything / everyone / everywhere
points.summary: Question word + 都 (+ 不) = every- / (not) any-.
points.body:
- 我**什么都**不想做.
- 他**谁都**认识.
examples: I don't feel like doing anything.

notes: 张 is for flat things like paper.
条 is for trousers, not clothes in general.
questions.translation: I bought two pieces of clothing.

notes: 件 is for clothes and matters.
questions.translation: There are three sheets of paper on the table.
Waiter, a cup of coffee, please.

questions.prompt: {我|wǒ}{买|mǎi}{了|le}（　）{本|běn}{书|shū}，{都|dōu}{很|hěn}{有意思|yǒu yìsi}。
notes: 有的 doesn't take a measure word.
一些 doesn't take a measure word: 一些书.
questions.translation: I bought a few books — they're all interesting.

questions.prompt: In 「{我|wǒ}{有|yǒu}{几|jǐ}{个|ge}{中国|Zhōngguó}{朋友|péngyou}。」, what does 几 mean?
notes: In a statement (。), 几 isn't a question.
questions.translation: I have a few Chinese friends.

notes: 都 comes after the 每 phrase.
questions.translation: Each of us has a book.

questions.prompt: {我|wǒ}{在|zài}{这儿|zhèr}{等|děng}{了|le}{一个|yí ge}（　）{小时|xiǎoshí}。
notes: 一个半个 has one 个 too many.
questions.translation: I've been waiting here for an hour and a half.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'half an hour'?
notes: 一半 = 'a half (portion)', not before a measure.

questions.prompt: How do you say ¥3.50 in everyday speech?
notes: Prices aren't said like that — 五 after 块 already means 5 毛 (50 fen).

questions.prompt: （　）{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{喝|hē}{茶|chá}，{有的|yǒude}{人|rén}{喜欢|xǐhuan}{喝|hē}{咖啡|kāfēi}。
notes: The contrast pattern is 有的…，有的….
questions.translation: Some people like tea, some like coffee.

notes: 有的 picks some out of a group — not an amount to buy.
questions.translation: I want to go to the supermarket to buy some fruit.

notes: 哪 needs a measure word / 儿.
怎么都不想做 = 'no matter how, I don't want to' — not 'anything'.
谁 = 'anyone' — but 做 needs a thing.
questions.translation: I'm so tired, I don't feel like doing anything.

questions.prompt: {他|tā}{朋友|péngyou}{很|hěn}{多|duō}，{学校|xuéxiào}{里|lǐ}（　）{都|dōu}{认识|rènshi}{他|tā}。
notes: 什么 = 'anything' — people know him, not things.
questions.translation: He has lots of friends — everyone at school knows him.
